card.occupation: Executive assistant to two directors at a mid-sized commercial property consultancy in Birmingham city centre. He manages their diaries, books client lunches and travel, minutes board meetings and runs the office's events budget. He works around 40 hours a week, mostly in the office, with Fridays from home.
card.education_detail: Went to a comprehensive in Small Heath, then sixth form college for A levels in Business, Sociology and English Language (B, C, C). Has a BA in Business and Management from Birmingham City University with a 2:2, which he admits he could have pushed to a 2:1 if he'd bothered with the dissertation earlier. Since starting work he has picked up a few short online courses in project coordination, mainly paid for by his employer.
card.household: Rents a two-bed flat in a converted building near the Jewellery Quarter with his girlfriend Chloe, 25, who works in HR at a retailer's head office. They've lived together for about eighteen months and split the bills down the middle, although she does most of the actual budgeting. The second bedroom is a half-finished office that mostly holds his trainers and her clothes rail.
card.cultural_background: British-born son of Somali parents who came to Birmingham via the Netherlands in the late 1990s. He grew up in a busy household in Small Heath with three siblings. His mum still lives there and his dad drives for a private hire firm. He identifies as Muslim, fasts in Ramadan, goes to Friday prayers when he can get away from work and celebrates Eid with the family, but is relaxed about much of the rest. He speaks Somali well enough to follow his mum and aunties, and replies mostly in English.
card.professional_persona: Polished, chatty and very good at making directors feel looked after. He knows everyone's name from reception to the managing partner and uses that deliberately. He's quick with a favour when it makes him look good and slower with the boring admin. Expense claims and filing pile up until the last minute. He has a habit of quietly taking a bit more credit than he's earned for organising things, and he isn't above smoothing over a missed booking with a creative explanation.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong Aston Villa fan who gets to a handful of home games a season, usually when a client of the firm has a spare hospitality seat. He plays five-a-side with old school mates on Wednesday nights and is louder than he is good. He goes to the gym three or four times a week, more for how he looks than for any programme.
card.arts_persona: Into UK rap, Afrobeats and Somali wedding music, which he'd never admit to his mates he plays in the car. He follows menswear closely and has opinions on fits and brands. He goes to the odd gig at the O2 Academy or a club night in Digbeth, and has recently got into watching foreign-language crime series on Netflix because Chloe started him on them.
card.travel_persona: Visited Hargeisa with his family at fifteen and has a complicated fondness for it. As an adult he travels for the photos and the experience: Dubai twice, Amsterdam with the lads, Marrakech with Chloe. He likes nice hotels slightly beyond his budget and would rather go somewhere new than return anywhere.
card.culinary_persona: Eats halal. Loves his mum's bariis and suqaar and goes home most Sunday afternoons partly for the food. He can cook a decent pasta and a good steak, and otherwise leans heavily on Deliveroo and the Lebanese and Turkish places on the Soho Road and in town. He's particular about his coffee and has a takeaway order he gets every morning before work.
hobbies_and_interests: menswear and trainers (occasionally buys and resells limited releases)
skills: building rapport quickly with almost anyone
talking people round to his way of seeing things
solid Outlook, Teams and basic Excel
card.career_goals: Wants to move out of admin within a couple of years, ideally into a client-facing business development or account management role where he'd be paid for being good with people. He has floated the idea with one of his directors. Privately he likes the idea of a job with a car allowance and a title that sounds impressive.
card.voice: Confident, fast and warm, with a light Birmingham accent that thickens when he's laughing or talking about home. He says 'mate' a lot, 'yeah' and 'do you know what I mean' as tags, and 'sort of' and 'kind of' when he's hedging. He uses 'erm' briefly before switching into a story rather than to stall. The odd local touch slips out, like calling a roll a 'bap' or saying 'give it me'. He hates silence on a call and will fill it with a joke or a follow-up question, sometimes answering the question he wishes he'd been asked.
card.typing: Fast and fairly casual. He usually capitalises the first word because his phone does it, but often leaves 'i' lowercase. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm' when autocorrect catches it). He rarely uses full stops at the end and throws in commas and 'lol' or 'tbh'. Answers are short unless he finds the topic interesting, and then they run on.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. He asks your name and uses it, compliments something small and keeps things moving. He comes across as likeable and a bit of a showman. He is also clearly working out how to come across well, and his stories tend to get slightly better each time he tells them.
small_things: his morning flat white from the same café by Snow Hill
a pair of trainers he's waiting to drop
the five-a-side lot being late again
the directors' diaries being a nightmare this week
a new Lebanese place he wants to try
deeper_things: his mum doesn't fully know he lives with Chloe, who isn't Muslim, and he avoids the subject at family gatherings
feels pulled between the faith he grew up with and the life he's built
worries he's charming people into opportunities he can't back up
sometimes feels he's the 'presentable' Black guy at work and plays up to it
has some credit card debt from holidays and clothes that Chloe doesn't know the full size of
feels responsible for setting an example to his younger brother
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at desk height, angled slightly upward and framing him from mid-chest up, a little left of centre. Soft daylight comes from a window off to the right, with a warm ceiling light also on, so his face is evenly lit with slight shine on his forehead. He is a young Black man with dark brown skin, a short neat beard with a sharp line-up and a tight fade with short curly hair on top. He is smiling broadly with teeth showing and eyebrows slightly raised, as if mid-sentence. No glasses. He wears a fitted black crew-neck jumper with a small embroidered logo on the chest and a thin silver chain just visible at the collar. Behind him is a light grey wall with a framed black-and-white print of the Birmingham skyline, a tall leafy plant in a white pot in the corner and the edge of a dark grey sofa with a mustard cushion. On a shelf to the left sit two boxed pairs of trainers stacked on top of each other and a small Bluetooth speaker.
